free_tier.stated: AMD-only GPU host, one model: MI300X at USD 2.99 per GPU-hour on demand, checked 2026-10-22 and unchanged since 2026-10-15. Third-party billing facts, each attributed to the vendor's own pages: billing per minute, minimum rental of one GPU for one minute, and prepaid credits bought by card through Stripe or in USDT and USDC.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The one-minute minimum and per-minute billing make this the only 192 GB card sold in units a benchmark can afford, which is what a trial run needs before a multi-hour commitment.
limits_note: Nothing published binds above a single GPU for a single minute; the whole cost is prepaid and the smallest unit is one minute.
binding_note: Nothing published binds above a single GPU for a single minute; the whole cost is prepaid and the smallest unit is one minute.

identity_cost.detail: Prepaid credits rather than a subscription, and the tracker records payment by card or by USDT and USDC, so a stablecoin balance is an alternative to a card.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'Hot Aisle rents 1 GPU model today, from $2.99 an hour (MI300X, on-demand)'; source of the rate given as hotaisle.xyz/pricing
quoted billing terms: 'Billing is per minute', 'Minimum rental time: one GPU for one minute', 'prepaid credits by card (Stripe) or USDT and USDC', each checked on 2026-10-17
MI300X market median across 5 providers is USD 2.99/hr, so Hot Aisle matches the median rather than undercutting it

notes: Storage price, data-out price and the rule for stopped instances are stated by the tracker as unpublished by the vendor, which matters because a 192 GB card implies a large dataset beside it.
